description: A row of stored values that you draw with the mouse, record into or load from a wav file, and read out with a voltage that moves a cursor along it

params.text: Sets the voltage span that sweeps a cursor from the start of the array to the end, +10V, ±5V or ±10V, and applies to POS and REC POS alike
Sets the voltage span that the bottom and top of the array stand for, +10V, ±5V or ±10V, and applies to the signal being recorded and to both outputs
Writes REC IN into the array while the button is held, or starts and stops the recording at each click when the recording mode is Toggle; it glows while recording

inputs.text: Moves the playback cursor along the array, the bottom of the range set by POS RANGE reading the first value and the top the last; a polyphonic cable gives every channel its own cursor
The signal written into the array while recording, read over the span set by I/O RANGE and clipped to it
Sets the point in the array that a recorded value is written to, read over the span set by POS RANGE
A high gate records REC IN for as long as it lasts, or a rising edge starts and stops the recording when the recording mode is Toggle; it reads high above 2V

outputs.text: Carries the stored value under the cursor with no smoothing, stepping from one value to the next
Carries the value under the cursor smoothed with a four-point curve through the neighbouring values, the same interpolation the tabread4~ object in Pure Data uses

notes: drag across the display with the mouse to draw the array; the pointer's height sets the value under it, and a fast drag draws a straight line through the values it passes over
the number under SIZE is how many values the array holds; click it and type a new one, up to 999999, and new values are added at 0V
recording is monophonic: only the first channel of REC IN and REC POS is read, however many the cable carries
the array comes up holding ten values rising evenly from the bottom to the top, and Reset array contents on the menu puts them back
bypassing the module passes REC IN straight to both outputs
loading a wav file locks drawing, and Disable drawing on the menu unlocks it again
menu: Reset array contents — replaces the array with ten values rising evenly from the bottom to the top
Set array contents to zero — sets every value in the array to 0V, keeping its length
Sort array contents — reorders the values already in the array into a rising ramp
Add fade in/out to prevent clicks — fades the start and the end of the array towards 0V, over the number of values printed beside the item
Disable drawing — stops the mouse from changing the array, which loading a wav file switches on by itself
Recording mode: Gate, Toggle — chooses whether the REC input and button record while they are high or held, or start and stop the recording at each rising edge and click
Load .wav file... — reads a wav file into the array, keeping the current SIZE and filling only that many values, with the duration of the present array printed beside the item
Load .wav file and resize array... — reads a wav file into the array and sets SIZE to the length of the file, up to 999999 values
Data persistence: Save full array data to patch file, Save path to loaded sample, Don't save array data — chooses what the patch stores of the array
Interpolation at boundary: Constant, Mirror, Periodic — chooses what the smooth output reads past the ends of the array: the end value held, the array folded back, or the array repeated

inputs.3:
high above 2V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
